PART 1 — BASICS OF NURSING CARE
PART 1 — CHAPTER 1
මානව ගෞරවය සහ ස්වාධීනත්වය
මෙම පාඩමේ මූලික අදහස වන්නේ සත්කාරය ලබන සෑමෙ පුද්ගලයකුමෙ වයස, රෝගය හෝ ආබාධය නිසා
තම ගෞරවය සහ අයිතිවාසිකමේ අහිමි නොකරන බවයි. ඔහුගේ හෝ ඇයගේ ජීවන රටාව, වටිනාකම්,
කැමැත්ත, සංස්කෘතිය සහ තීරණ ගැනීමේ හැකියාව සලකා සත්කාරය සැලසුම් කළ යුතුය. QOL යනු
ජීවිතයේ ගුණාත්මෙකභාවයයි. Normalization යනු හැකි තරමේ සාමාන්‍ය සමොජ ජීවිතයක් ගත කිරීමට සහාය
වීමයි. Self-determination යනු පුද්ගලයාට තම තීරණ ගැනීමෙට ඉඩ දීමෙයි. පුද්ගලයාට තනිව කළ හැකි දේ
සත්කාර ස්වකයා ඔහු වනුවන් නොකළ යුතුය.
HUMAN DIGNITY AND INDEPENDENCE IN NURSING CARE
人間の尊厳と自立 / මානව ගෞරවය සහ ස්වාධීනත්වය
1. HUMAN DIGNITY
🇯🇵 人間の尊厳（にんげんのそんげん）
🇬🇧 Human dignity
🇱🇰 මානව ගෞරවය
Core idea:
Every person must be respected as an individual. A person does not lose dignity or rights because they become
elderly, disabled, ill, or need nursing care.
Important:
• Respect the person's values and lifestyle.
• Protect the person's rights.
• Do not treat a user as an object of care.
• Do not impose the caregiver's personal values.
• Protect privacy and dignity during personal care.
2. USER-CENTERED CARE
🇯🇵 利用者中心
🇬🇧 User-centered care
🇱🇰 ස්වාලාභියා කේන්ද්‍ර කරගත් සත්කාරය
The user's lifestyle, values, preferences, habits, culture and wishes must be considered.
Examples:
• Ask which clothes the user wants.
• Respect preferred daily routines.
• Respect food preferences.
• Respect personal habits.
• Support the person rather than controlling the person.

3. QUALITY OF LIFE — QOL
🇯🇵 生活の質（QOL）
🇬🇧 Quality of Life
🇱🇰 ජීවන තත්ත්වය
QOL includes:
• Physical comfort
• Mental well-being
• Satisfaction
• Happiness
• Meaningful daily life
• Relationships
• Ability to make choices
4. NORMALIZATION
🇯🇵 ノーマライゼーション
🇬🇧 Normalization
🇱🇰 සාමාන්‍යකරණය
People with disabilities should be able to live ordinary lives in society while their human rights and individuality
are respected.
5. SELF-INDEPENDENCE / SELF-DETERMINATION
🇯🇵 自立 / 自己決定
🇬🇧 Independence / self-determination
🇱🇰 ස්වාධීනත්වය / ස්වයං තීරණය
Two important dimensions:
• Physical independence
• Mental / decision-making independence
The user's own decision should be respected whenever possible.
6. INDEPENDENCE SUPPORT
🇯🇵 自立支援（じりつしえん）
🇬🇧 Support for independence
🇱🇰 ස්වාධීනත්වයට සහාය
Golden rule:
DO NOT do automatically what the user can still do.
Support only where needed and allow the user to perform the parts they can perform.
Care sequence:

1. Observe the user's condition.
2. Determine what the user can do.
3. Encourage the user to do it independently.
4. Assist only where necessary.
5. Maintain safety.
EXAM TRAP:
"Care worker does everything because it is faster" = incorrect when the user can perform the activity safely.
PART 1 — CHAPTER 2
වෘත්තීය ආචාරධර්ම සහ රහස්‍යභාවය
පෞද්ගලිකත්වය, රහස්‍යභාවය සහ පුද්ගල ගෞරවය ආරක්ෂා කිරීමෙ අත්‍යවශ්‍යය. පෞද්ගලික තොරතුරු
අවසර නොමැති පුද්ගලයන්ට හළි නොකළ යුතුය. ශාරීරික, මානසික, නොසලකා හැරීමෙ, ආර්ථික සහ
ලිංගික අපයෝජන හඳුනාගත යුතුය. Physical restraint අනවශ්‍ය ලස භාවිතා නොකළ යුතුය. වෘත්තීය සීමො
තුළ වැඩ කරමින් වනත් විශේෂඥයන් සමෙඟ කණ්ඩායමේ ලස කටයුතු කළ යුතුය.
ROLE AND PROFESSIONAL ETHICS OF CARE WORKERS
介護職の役割と職業倫理 / සත්කාර ස්වකයාගේ භූමිකාව හා වෘත්තීය ආචාරධර්මෙ
1. ROLE OF THE CARE WORKER
🇯🇵 介護職（かいごしょく）
🇬🇧 Care worker
🇱🇰 සත්කාර ස්වකයා
Care workers:
• Support daily living.
• Respect dignity.
• Support independence.
• Observe changes.
• Record and report.
• Work as part of a team.
• Protect users' privacy.
• Provide safe nursing care within their role.
2. PRIVACY
🇯🇵 プライバシー
🇬🇧 Privacy
🇱🇰 පෞද්ගලිකත්වය
Protect privacy especially during:
• Toileting

3. Encourage the user to do it independently.

3. CONFIDENTIALITY / DUTY OF SECRECY
🇯🇵 守秘義務（しゅひぎむ）
🇬🇧 Confidentiality / duty of confidentiality
🇱🇰 රහස්‍යභාවය / රහස්‍ය තොරතුරු ආරක්ෂා කිරීමෙ
Do not disclose a user's personal information to unauthorized people.
Examples of personal information:
• Name
• Address
• Age
• Health information
• Family information
• Care information
Do not publish user information or photographs on social media without appropriate permission.
4. PHYSICAL RESTRAINT PROHIBITION
🇯🇵 身体拘束の禁止
🇬🇧 Prohibition of physical restraint
🇱🇰 ශාරීරික සීමො කිරීමෙ තහනමේ කිරීමෙ
Examples:
• Tying hands or feet
• Using bed rails in a way that prevents the person from getting out
• Locking the room to prevent leaving
• Using a belt to prevent standing
• Excessive use of psychotropic medication as restraint
Potential harm:
• Physical deterioration
• Reduced physical ability
• Psychological distress
• Worsening dementia-related symptoms
5. ABUSE
🇯🇵 虐待（ぎゃくたい）
🇬🇧 Abuse
🇱🇰 අපයෝජනය
Types:

A. 身体的虐待 — Physical abuse — ශාරීරික අපයෝජනය
B. 心理的虐待 — Psychological abuse — මානසික අපයෝජනය
C. ネグレクト — Neglect — නොසලකා හැරීමෙ
D. 経済的虐待 — Economic abuse — ආර්ථික අපයෝජනය
E. 性的虐待 — Sexual abuse — ලිංගික අපයෝජනය
6. TEAM APPROACH
🇯🇵 多職種連携
🇬🇧 Interprofessional collaboration
🇱🇰 බහු-වෘත්තීය සහයරෝගීතාව
Possible professionals:
• Doctor 医師
• Nurse 看護師
• Care worker 介護職
• Care manager 介護支援専門員
• Social worker 社会福祉士
• Dietitian 栄養士
• Physical therapist 理学療法士
• Occupational therapist 作業療法士
• Speech-language therapist 言語聴覚士
• Dentist 歯科医師
Important:
Care workers must work within their professional role and cooperate with medical and other specialists.

ENSURING SAFETY AND RISK MANAGEMENT
安全・リスク管理 / ආරක්ෂාව හා අවදානමේ කළමෙනොකරණය
1. TYPES OF CARE SERVICES
🇯🇵 
訪問介護 — Home-visit care
通所介護 — Day care
施設介護 — Facility/institutional care

2. CARE PROCESS
🇯🇵 介護過程
🇬🇧 Care process
🇱🇰 සත්කාර කික්‍රියාවලිය
Basic flow:
1. Assessment アセスメント
2. Care plan 介護計画
3. Implementation 実施
4. Evaluation 評価
Assessment:
Collect information and understand the user's problems, needs and abilities.
Care plan:
Set goals and decide appropriate support.
Implementation:
Provide care according to the plan.
Evaluation:
Check the result and whether the plan needs adjustment.
3. OBSERVATION
🇯🇵 観察（かんさつ）
🇬🇧 Observation
🇱🇰 නිරීක්ෂණය
Observe:
• Facial expression
• Speech
• Behavior
• Physical condition
• Temperature
• Blood pressure
• Changes from normal condition
• Skin condition
• Eating and elimination
• Pain or discomfort
Report significant changes promptly.
4. ACCIDENT PREVENTION
Before care:
• Check physical condition.

• Check environment.
• Check footwear and clothing.
• Check equipment.
• Check wheelchair brakes.
• Remove hazards.
• Explain the procedure.
5. RISK MANAGEMENT
🇯🇵 リスクマネジメント
🇬🇧 Risk management
🇱🇰 අවදානමේ කළමෙනොකරණය
Basic cycle:
Predict danger → prevent accident → observe → record → report/share → prevent recurrence.
6. INFECTION CONTROL
🇯🇵 感染対策
🇬🇧 Infection control
🇱🇰 ආසාදන පාලනය
Three elements:
• Infectious agent / source
• Route of transmission
• Susceptible host
Basic principles:
• Do not bring infection in.
• Do not take infection out.
• Do not spread infection.
7. STANDARD PRECAUTIONS
🇯🇵 標準予防策
🇬🇧 Standard precautions
🇱🇰 සමේමෙත ආරක්ෂණ ක්‍රිමෙ
Treat blood and potentially infectious body fluids, secretions, excretions, mucous membranes and non-intact
skin as potentially infectious.
8. PPE
• Disposable gloves 使い捨て手袋
• Mask マスク
• Goggles / eye protection
• Apron エプロン
• Other appropriate protective equipment

9. HAND HYGIENE
🇯🇵 手洗い / 手指衛生
🇬🇧 Hand hygiene
🇱🇰 අත් සනීපාරක්ෂාව
Basic handwashing sequence:
1. Wet hands.
2. Apply liquid soap.
3. Rub palms.
4. Wash backs of hands.
5. Wash between fingers.
6. Wash thumbs.
7. Wash fingertips/nails.
8. Wash wrists.
9. Rinse thoroughly.
10. Dry completely.
10. DISPOSABLE GLOVES
🇯🇵 使い捨て手袋
🇬🇧 Disposable gloves
🇱🇰 එක්වර භාවිතා කරන අත්වැසුමේ
Rules:
• Use appropriately.
• Change between users/care situations as required.
• Do not reuse disposable gloves.
• Perform hand hygiene after removal.
11. BODY MECHANICS
🇯🇵 ボディメカニクス
🇬🇧 Body mechanics
🇱🇰 ශරීර යාන්ත්‍ර විද්‍යාව
Key principles:
• Widen the base of support.
• Lower the center of gravity.
• Bring the user's center of gravity close.

• Use large muscle groups.
• Use leverage.
• Avoid twisting the trunk.
• Move the center of gravity efficiently.
• Pull/slide rather than unnecessarily lift when appropriate.
Japanese key term:
てこの原理 — Principle of leverage — ලීවර මූලධර්මෙය
12. LOWER-BACK PAIN PREVENTION
🇯🇵 腰痛予防
🇬🇧 Lower-back pain prevention
🇱🇰 පහළ පිටුපස වේදනාව වැළැක්වීමෙ
Important:
• Adjust bed height.
• Maintain stable posture.
• Use body mechanics.
• Avoid twisting.
• Use equipment when appropriate.
• Do not rely on excessive physical force.
13. CARE WORKER HEALTH
Care workers also need health management, rest, safe working methods and appropriate consultation when
physical problems occur.

• Mobilize out of bed where possible.
• Reposition regularly.
• Maintain nutrition.
• Observe skin.
• Report redness or skin problems.

10. BASIC TRANSFER PRINCIPLES
Always:

1. Confirm physical condition.
2. Explain what you will do.
3. Obtain consent.
4. Adjust bed height.
5. Support independence.
6. Continue observation.
Do not force movement when physical condition is poor. Report concerns to appropriate medical staff.
11. TURNING IN BED — HEMIPLEGIA EXAMPLE
General sequence:
1. Confirm condition.
2. Explain.
3. Obtain consent.
4. Adjust bed.
5. Raise knees as appropriate.
6. Have user assume lateral position with affected side.
7. Move lower back toward the other side as needed.
8. Position limbs comfortably.
9. Tuck arms/legs closer to the center to make the base of support smaller/stable.
10. Confirm comfort.
12. GETTING UP FROM BED
• Confirm condition.
• Explain.
• Obtain consent.
• Adjust bed height.
• Sit user at bed edge.
• Ensure both feet/soles are stable.
• Move legs off the bed.
• Assist upper body.
• Confirm dizziness/pain.
• Confirm readiness to stand.
13. STANDING
• Ask user to sit near edge.
• Care worker positions safely.

Two-point and three-point patterns are described in the source.

The cane provides support while the affected leg needs additional assistance.

1. Cane
2. Unaffected foot
3. Affected foot

• Check tire pressure.

1. Confirm condition.
2. Explain.
3. Obtain consent.
4. Sit user at bed edge.
5. Position wheelchair beside unaffected side.
6. Apply wheelchair brake.
7. User holds far armrest with unaffected hand.

Meals:
• Provide nutrients.
• Sustain bodily functions.
• Help establish daily rhythm.
• Provide enjoyment.
• Stimulate the brain through taste and eating.
• Provide an opportunity for communication.
2. SWALLOWING / EATING FLOW

🇯🇵 先行期
🇬🇧 Anticipatory stage
🇱🇰 ආහාරය හඳුනාගැනීමේ පර අවධිය

🇱🇰 උගුර් අවධිය

🇬🇧 Esophageal stage
🇱🇰 අන්නනාල අවධිය

5. MEALTIME PRECAUTIONS
Before:
• Confirm food preference.
• Check allergies.

• Check medical/treatment restrictions.
• Confirm chewing/swallowing ability.
• Prepare suitable food consistency.
• Serve warm food warm and cold food cold as appropriate.
6. CORRECT POSTURE
• Sit with back supported.
• Both soles on floor where possible.
• Lean slightly forward.
• Draw chin slightly inward.
• Avoid lifting the chin upward because aspiration risk can increase.
7. EATING IN BED
If sitting is difficult:
• Raise upper body.
• Use a semi-sitting position.
• Perform senuki after raising the upper body.
• If needed, use pillows.
• In hemiplegia, position with unaffected side down when indicated by the source.

2. Explain.
3. Obtain consent.
4. Clean user's hands.
5. Bring user to table/chair.
6. Place meal where user can see/reach.
7. Care worker sits at appropriate position.
8. Confirm allergy/treatment restrictions.
9. Allow user to eat at their pace.
10. Observe chewing and swallowing.
11. Adjust support.
12. Prevent aspiration.
13. Confirm after-meal condition.
14. Provide oral care as needed.
15. Maintain appropriate posture after meal.

🇱🇰 මෙල පිට කිරීමෙ

4. DEFECATION POSTURE
A stable seated posture with slight forward leaning helps make elimination easier.
5. URINARY INCONTINENCE
🇯🇵 尿失禁
🇬🇧 Urinary incontinence
🇱🇰 මුත්‍රා අසංයමෙය

Stress incontinence:
Leakage caused by increased abdominal pressure such as coughing or sneezing.

7. TOILETING ASSISTANCE
• Explain.
• Obtain consent.
• Protect privacy.
• Use curtains/door.
• Provide appropriate support.
• Allow independence.
• Observe urine/feces.
• Record/report abnormal findings.
8. GENITAL / PERINEAL CLEANING
Key direction:
FRONT → BACK
URETHRA → ANUS
Do not wipe from anus toward urethra.
Use appropriate disposable gloves and protect privacy.
9. DIAPER CHANGE
General sequence:
• Explain.
• Prepare equipment.
• Protect privacy.
• Wear gloves.
• Remove soiled diaper.
• Observe urine/feces/skin.
• Clean from front to back as appropriate.
• Apply clean diaper.
• Confirm comfort.
• Dispose of waste safely.
• Hand hygiene.
• Record/report abnormalities.
10. CONSTIPATION / DIARRHEA
Observe:
• Frequency
• Amount
• Color
• Form
• Smell
• Blood/mucus
• Pain
• Changes from normal
Report concerning abnormalities.

ඇඳුමේ ගලවන විට — බලපෑමෙක් නැති පැත්ත මුලින්.
ඇඳුමේ අන්දවන විට — බලපෑමෙට ලක් වූ පැත්ත මුලින්.
4. DRESSING PROCEDURE
• Confirm sitting stability.
• Explain.
• Support affected arm/leg.
• Undress unaffected side first.
• Dress affected side first.

• Avoid excessive pulling.
• Confirm comfort and physical condition.
5. PANTS
When removing:
• Unaffected side first.
When putting on:
• Affected side first.
If the user can raise the lower back:
• Ask the user to do it.
• Support independence.
6. HAIR CARE
🇯🇵 整髪 / 髪をとかす
🇬🇧 Hair grooming
🇱🇰 හිසකස් සකස් කිරීමෙ
Use comb appropriately and respect hairstyle preference.
7. SHAVING
🇯🇵 ひげそり
🇬🇧 Shaving
🇱🇰 රැවුල කැපීමෙ
Electric razor:
• Hold at right angle to skin.
• Lightly stretch skin/wrinkles.
• Check for remaining stubble.
• Protect skin with shaving lotion when appropriate.
8. NAIL CARE
🇯🇵 爪きり
🇬🇧 Nail clipping
🇱🇰 නිය කැපීමෙ
Important:
• Nails become softer after bathing.
• Clip when appropriately softened.
• Observe nails and surrounding skin.
• Report abnormalities.
• Long nails can damage skin and harbor dirt.

9. ORAL CARE
🇯🇵 口腔ケア
🇬🇧 Oral care
🇱🇰 මුඛ සත්කාර
Benefits:
• Prevent dental caries.
• Prevent periodontal disease.
• Reduce oral bacteria.
• Reduce bad breath.
• Help prevent aspiration pneumonia.
• Prevent dry mouth.
• Promote saliva.
• Maintain taste/appetite.
10. TOOTHBRUSHING
• Confirm condition.
• User rinses mouth first.
• Use appropriate toothbrush.
• Use short/light strokes.
• Observe oral cavity.
• Be careful around affected areas.
• Report bleeding/swelling.
11. SPONGE BRUSH
Can be used appropriately for oral cleaning where indicated.
12. DENTURES
🇯🇵 義歯 / 入れ歯
🇬🇧 Dentures
🇱🇰 කෘති්‍රමෙ දත්
After meals:
• Remove appropriately.
• Clean with appropriate brush/running water.
• Store in water or denture-cleaning solution as appropriate.
• Do not allow dentures to dry.
• Clean remaining oral structures.

PART 4 — CHAPTER 5
Bathing සහ cleanliness
Bathing සඳහා privacy, physical condition සහ environmental safety සලකා බලන්න. Dressing room සහ
bathroom අතර temperature difference අඩු කිරීමෙ heat shock අවදානමෙ අඩු කරයි. Wet floors සහ level
differences fall risk වේ. Female genital cleaning front → back. Bed bath order: face → arms → chest/abdomen
→ back → legs → genital area.

Benefits:
• Cleanliness
• Comfort
• Relaxation
• Blood circulation
• Skin care
• Psychological refreshment
• Daily rhythm
2. SKIN FUNCTIONS
🇯🇵 皮膚の機能
🇬🇧 Functions of skin
🇱🇰 සමේ කාර්යයන්
• Protect internal organs.
• Prevent harmful stimulation.
• Moisturize using sweat/sebum.
• Regulate body temperature.
3. SWEAT GLANDS
Eccrine gland:
🇯🇵 エクリン腺
🇬🇧 Eccrine gland
🇱🇰 එක්රින් දහඩිය ග්‍රන්ථිය
Apocrine gland:
🇯🇵 アポクリン腺
🇬🇧 Apocrine gland
🇱🇰 ඇපාක්‍රියින් දහඩිය ග්‍රන්ථිය

Prevent large temperature differences between dressing room and bathroom.
6. BEFORE BATHING
• Confirm condition.
• Explain.
• Obtain consent.
• Prepare environment.
• Prepare clothes.
• Encourage toilet use when appropriate.
• Consider hydration.
• Confirm appropriate timing.
• Check for contraindications/health concerns and report as needed.
7. WATER TEMPERATURE
• Check safely.
• Allow user to confirm where possible.
• Start water appropriately.
• Gradually move from extremities toward central areas as described by the source.
• Avoid burns.
8. WASHING
• Use liquid soap appropriately.
• Wash gently.
• Avoid excessive rubbing.
• Pay attention to skin folds and dirty areas.
• Protect privacy.
• Support affected side.
9. GETTING OUT OF BATH
Risk:

Orthostatic hypotension.
Therefore:
• Do not rush standing.
• Support the user.
• Observe dizziness.
• Confirm condition.
10. HAIR WASHING
• Protect eyes/ears as needed.
• Use shampoo.
• Use fingertips/finger pads.
• DO NOT scratch scalp with fingernails.
• Rinse properly.
• Dry safely.
11. AFTER BATH
• Dry gently.
• Pat/press rather than harsh rubbing.
• Dry skin folds.
• Moisturize as appropriate.
• Dress.
• Dry hair safely.
• Encourage appropriate fluid intake.
• Allow rest.
Hair dryer:
Keep a hand between warm air and the user's skin to prevent burns.
12. GENITAL CLEANING
• Protect privacy.
• Use appropriate warm water.
• Wear disposable gloves.
• Clean gently.
• Female: front to back / urethra toward anus.
• Observe redness or skin abnormalities.
• Report concerns.
13. BED BATH
General body sequence in the source:

1. Face
2. Arms
3. Chest
4. Back
5. Legs
6. Genital area

• Independent living
• Safe living
• Clean environment
• Healthy lifestyle
• User participation
2. COOKING
Basic sequence:
1. Decide menu.
2. Prepare ingredients.
3. Cook.
4. Plate food.
5. Set table.
6. Clean up / wash dishes.
Consider:
• User's condition.
• Disease.
• Allergies.

• Dietary restrictions.
• Preferences.
• Ability.

Goal:
Safe, clean, comfortable environment.
Important:
Do not throw away or relocate belongings merely because the caregiver considers them unnecessary.
Ask the user and obtain agreement where appropriate.

• Type of clothing.
• Fabric.
• User's preferences.
• Hygiene.
• Contamination.

• Handle appropriately.
• Separate from ordinary laundry when required.
• Follow infection-control procedure.

HIGH-YIELD PROCEDURE MEMORY SHEET
1. CARE PROCESS
Assessment → Care plan → Implementation → Evaluation
アセスメント → 介護計画 → 実施 → 評価
2. HANDWASHING
Wet → Soap → Palms → Backs → Between fingers → Thumbs → Fingertips → Wrists → Rinse → Dry
3. DRESSING / UNDRESSING
脱健着患
Undress: unaffected side first.
Dress: affected side first.
4. FEMALE PERINEAL CLEANING
Front → back.
Urethra → anus.
5. STAIRS
UP:
Cane → unaffected leg → affected leg.
DOWN:
Cane → affected leg → unaffected leg.
6. SWALLOWING
Anticipatory → Preparatory → Oral → Pharyngeal → Esophageal
先行期 → 準備期 → 口腔期 → 咽頭期 → 食道期
7. PRESSURE ULCER
Risk areas:
Skull / scapula / elbow / sacrum / buttocks / heel.
8. WHEELCHAIR
Check tires + brakes.
Brake ON when stationary.
Tell user before movement.
Keep hands/feet safely positioned.

9. BODY MECHANICS
Wide base + low center of gravity + close center of gravity + large muscles + leverage + no twisting.
10. DEMENTIA
Do not simply deny.
Listen → accept → reassure → simple language → maintain familiar routine.
11. RECORDING
When / Where / Who / What / Why / How
いつ / どこで / だれが / 何を / なぜ / どのように
12. MEAL POSTURE
Back supported + feet stable + slight forward lean + chin slightly down.
13. BATHING
Check condition + environment + water temperature + fall risk + heat shock.
After bath: dry gently + skin folds + hydration + observe dizziness.
14. INDEPENDENCE
Do not do what the user can safely do independently.
EXAM QUESTION PATTERNS TO MASTER
A. "Which is correct?"
Look for:
• Respect dignity
• Support independence
• Protect privacy
• Obtain consent
• Explain before care
• Observe condition
• Report abnormalities
• Use correct body mechanics
B. "Which is incorrect?"
Watch for:
• Doing everything for the user
• Ignoring user preference
• Sharing personal information
• Unnecessary restraint
• Ignoring abnormal symptoms
• Sudden movement
• Unsafe wheelchair handling
• Raising chin during swallowing
• Cleaning female genital area back-to-front
• Dressing affected side last
• Forgetting wheelchair brakes
C. PROCEDURE ORDER QUESTIONS

Memorize:
• Handwashing
• Care process
• Swallowing stages
• Bed-to-wheelchair transfer
• Stairs
• Dressing
• Genital cleaning
• Bathing
• Bed bath
• Cooking
• Recording/reporting
D. VOCABULARY QUESTIONS
Study Japanese + reading + English + Sinhala together.
E. SCENARIO QUESTIONS
Always ask:
1. What is the user's condition?
2. What is the risk?
3. What can the user still do?
4. What should the care worker explain?
5. Is consent needed?
6. What safety measure is required?
7. What should be observed?
8. What must be recorded/reported?

තමන්ටම øරීමට ඉඩ දන්න.
12. 無理をさせない — Do not force — බලන් නොකරවන්න.
13. 事故を予防する — Prevent accidents — අනතුරු වුළුක්වීම.

15. チームでケアする — Provide care as a team — කණ්ඩායමක් ලස සත්කාර කරන්න.

ENGLISH — SOURCE-VERIFIED
Normal urine volume: 1000–1500 mL per day.
Normal frequency: 4–6 times per day.
Polyuria: 2000–3000 mL per day or more.
Oliguria: 300–500 mL per day or less.
Pollakiuria: 8 times or more during the day, and 2 times or more at night.
Normal urine smell: no smell.   Abnormal smell: strong ammonia smell.
Normal colour: light yellow to transparent.   Abnormal colour: muddy, dark brown, red, etc.
සිංහල — මතක තබාගත යුතු සංඛ්‍යා

සාමාන්‍ය වාර ගණන: දිනකට 4–6 වාර.
අධික මුත්‍රා: දිනකට 2000–3000 මිලිලීටර් හෝ ඊට වැඩි.
අඩු මුත්‍රා: දිනකට 300–500 මිලිලීටර් හෝ ඊට අඩු.
නිතර මුත්‍රා කිරීම: දවල් 8 වාර හෝ වැඩි සහ රාත්‍රියේ 2 වාර හෝ වැඩි.

1. DISASTER PREPAREDNESS
災害への備え
ආපදා සූදානම
A disaster is an event that causes damage, such as an earthquake, typhoon, or fire. Facilities and local communities maintain a
cooperative disaster-response system. Preparation is important to avoid panic when a disaster occurs.
ආපදාවක් යනු භූමිකම්පා, ටයිෆූන් හෝ ගින්න වැනි හානි ඇති කරන සිදුවීමකි. පහසුකම්/ආයතන සහ ප්‍රාදේශීය
ප්‍රජාවන් සහයෝගී ආපදා ප්‍රතිචාර පද්ධතියක් පවත්වාගෙන යයි. ආපදාවකදී කලබලය වළක්වා ගැනීමට පෙර සූදානම
වැදගත්ය.
2. MASLOW’S HIERARCHY OF NEEDS
マズローの欲求階層
මැස්ලෝගේ අවශ්‍යතා ධූරාවලිය
Needs refer to a state of mind in which a person wants to get something. A. H. Maslow theorized that human needs consist of five levels:
physiological, safety, love/belonging, esteem, and self-actualization.
අවශ්‍යතාවක් යනු පුද්ගලයෙකුට යම් දෙයක් ලබාගැනීමට අවශ්‍ය වන මානසික තත්ත්වයකි. මැස්ලෝ අනුව මිනිස්
අවශ්‍යතා මට්ටම් 5කින් සමන්විත වේ: ශාරීරික, ආරක්ෂාව, ආදරය/අයත්භාවය, ගෞරවය සහ ස්වයං-සම්පූර්ණත්වය.
3. ALZHEIMER’S-TYPE DEMENTIA
アルツハイマー型認知症
ඇල්සයිමර් වර්ගයේ ඩිමෙන්ශියාව
The source lists dementia of the Alzheimer’s type among the causative diseases of dementia and states that Alzheimer’s-type dementia
progresses gradually. Retain this as an exam recognition point.
ඩිමෙන්ශියාව ඇති කරන රෝග අතර ඇල්සයිමර් වර්ගයේ ඩිමෙන්ශියාව ද ඇතුළත් වේ. ඇල්සයිමර් වර්ගයේ
ඩිමෙන්ශියාව ක්‍රමයෙන් වර්ධනය වන බව මූලාශ්‍රයේ සඳහන් වේ. මෙය විභාගයේ හඳුනාගැනීමේ කරුණක් ලෙස මතක
තබාගන්න.
4. HUMAN SPINE — S-SHAPED CURVE
脊柱のS字カーブ
මිනිස් කොඳු ඇට පෙළ — එස්-හැඩැති වක්‍රය
Physiologically, the human spine is curved in an S shape. The user’s exam-note record separately flags the S-shaped spine as a Lesson
2 exam point.
මිනිස් කොඳු ඇට පෙළ ශාරීරිකව එස්-හැඩයට වක්‍ර වී ඇත. ඔබගේ විභාග සටහන්වලද එස්-හැඩැති කොඳු ඇට පෙළ
පාඩම 2 හි විභාග කරුණක් ලෙස වෙනම සඳහන් කර ඇත.
